matches.rationale: Both identify a numerical inconsistency in the DDL-12 dataset size claims. GT_1 describes inflating the dataset size by roughly doubling, while pred_4 calculates that 2,050 images × 48 degradation variants should yield ~98,400 pairs, not the claimed ~52,800, revealing the same underlying data integrity issue.

GT_2 describes swapping query matrices between modalities in cross-attention (Q_vi with K_ir and Q_ir with K_vi), a specific method logic error. No finding addresses this cross-modal query swap or the conceptual inconsistency it introduces.

GT_3 identifies asymmetric experimental protocol where the proposed method uses SOTA restoration preprocessing while competitors do not. No finding discusses this unfair comparison or preprocessing asymmetry in Table 2.

GT_4 concerns overclaiming robustness and user-friendliness in the Introduction without acknowledging limitations. No finding addresses exaggerated claims about handling degradation scenarios or user flexibility.
GT_5 identifies fabrication of reference [8] (AutoDIR) as a non-existent paper. No finding discusses AutoDIR or fabricated references in the Related Work section.
GT_6 concerns the omission of ethical considerations in the Conclusion. No finding addresses missing ethical discussion, bias, or safety concerns.
GT_7 identifies promotional exaggeration in the Abstract ('outperforms SOTA') without caveats. No finding discusses rhetorical manipulation or overstated claims in the abstract.

GT_8 concerns inconsistency between claiming code availability in the Abstract but providing no details elsewhere. No finding addresses missing code access information or reproducibility documentation.

GT_9 identifies unclear application of loss functions (intensity, SSIM, gradient, color) in Stage II training. No finding discusses loss function specification or multi-objective optimization inconsistencies.

GT_10 concerns small batch size (12) and patch size (224×224) potentially limiting training robustness without discussion. No finding addresses experimental configuration choices or their implications.

GT_11 identifies selective interpretation where some metrics show mixed results but text claims dominance. Pred_5 discusses a different inconsistency (FLOPs vs. time percentages), not selective metric reporting.

GT_12 concerns overly optimistic framing of the degradation model's transferability in the Discussion. No finding addresses rhetorical manipulation or limitations acknowledgment in the discussion section.
GT_13 identifies fabricated 2025 publication dates for references [38] and [43]. No finding discusses anachronistic or temporally invalid references.
GT_14 concerns missing ethical considerations about datasets and safety-critical applications in the Experiments section. No finding addresses ethical omissions or responsible AI practices.

GT_15 identifies inconsistency between text claiming best performance on certain metrics while Table 3 shows Text-DiFuse outperforming on MUSIQ. No finding discusses this specific table-text mismatch in Section 5.3.
